case_name: Smt. Sunita v. Shri Rajendra — full case name

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: wife, mother of two minor children
parties.respondent_defendant: husband, father of two minor children

facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife claimed maintenance for herself and their two minor children. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A husband is under a legal obligation to maintain his wife, and this obligation continues even after the divorce.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that a husband is under a legal obligation to maintain his wife, and this obligation continues even after the divorce. The burden lies on the husband to prove that he is unable to pay the maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The court has the power to grant maintenance to a wife even after the divorce, if the husband is able to pay.
legal_principles.held: This court holds that it has the power to grant maintenance to a wife even after the divorce, if the husband is able to pay. The law is clear that the court can grant maintenance to a wife in such cases.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment of the trial court was upheld, directing the husband to pay maintenance to his wife and two minor children.
